title: The Holy Chambers for the Priests

questions.question: After the temple measurements, where was Ezekiel brought?
options: Out into the inner court, toward the north, to the chambers opposite the separate yard
To the outer court where the people gathered
To the city gates
To the river Chebar
questions.correctAnswer: Out into the inner court, toward the north, to the chambers opposite the separate yard
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:1 (ESV): "Then he led me out into the inner court, toward the north, and he brought me to the chambers that were opposite the separate yard..."

questions.question: How long was the building with the door facing north?
options: A hundred cubits long and fifty cubits broad
Fifty cubits long and fifty cubits broad
Two hundred cubits long
It was a perfect cube
questions.correctAnswer: A hundred cubits long and fifty cubits broad
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:2 (ESV): "The length of the building whose door faced north was a hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty cubits."

questions.question: How many stories did the galleries of these chambers have?
options: Three stories
Two stories
Five stories
Only one story
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:3 (ESV): "Gallery faced gallery in three stories."

questions.question: Why were the upper chambers narrower than the lower ones?
options: Because the galleries took away from them more than from the lower and middle chambers
Because they were built in the shape of a pyramid
Because the walls were thicker at the bottom
Because the roof was too heavy for a wide span
questions.correctAnswer: Because the galleries took away from them more than from the lower and middle chambers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:5 (ESV): "Now the upper chambers were narrower, for the galleries took more away from them than from the lower and middle chambers of the building."

questions.question: Did the buildings have pillars like the courts?
options: No, they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts
Yes, they had forty pillars on each side
Yes, bronze pillars at every corner
Yes, pillars carved as palm trees
questions.correctAnswer: No, they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:6 (ESV): "For they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts. Thus the upper chambers were set back from the ground more than the lower and the middle ones."

questions.question: What is the purpose of these north and south chambers facing the separate yard?
options: They are holy chambers where the priests who approach the Lord shall eat the most holy offerings
They are armories for the Levites
They are storage for the temple tithes
They are resting places for the pilgrims
questions.correctAnswer: They are holy chambers where the priests who approach the Lord shall eat the most holy offerings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:13 (ESV): "Then he said to me, 'The north chambers and the south chambers opposite the separate yard are the holy chambers, where the priests who approach the Lord shall eat the most holy offerings.'"

questions.question: Besides eating, what else are the priests to put in these holy chambers?
options: The most holy offerings—the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering
The golden vessels of the temple
The scrolls of the Prophet Jeremiah
The ashes from the brazen altar
questions.correctAnswer: The most holy offerings—the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:13 (ESV): "...There they shall put the most holy offerings—the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering—for the place is holy."

questions.question: When the priests leave the Holy Place, what must they do before going into the outer court where the people are?
options: They must leave their holy garments in which they ministered, for they are holy, and put on other garments
They must wash completely in the brazen sea
They must recite the Shema loudly
They must burn incense at the gate
questions.correctAnswer: They must leave their holy garments in which they ministered, for they are holy, and put on other garments
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:14 (ESV): "When the priests enter the Holy Place, they shall not go out of it into the outer court without laying there the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They shall put on other garments before they go near to that which is for the people."

questions.question: After finishing measuring the interior of the temple area, where did the man lead Ezekiel?
options: Out by the gate that faced east, to measure the temple area all around
Down to the river Chebar
To the Mount of Olives
Into the Most Holy Place again
questions.correctAnswer: Out by the gate that faced east, to measure the temple area all around
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:15 (ESV): "Now when he had finished measuring the interior of the temple area, he led me out by the gate that faced east, and measured the temple area all around."

questions.question: What measuring rod was used to measure the exterior sides?
options: The measuring reed
A line of flax
A golden plumb line
The cubit of the king
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:16 (ESV): "He measured the east side with the measuring reed, 500 cubits by the measuring reed all around."

questions.question: What were the full exterior dimensions of the temple area wall all around?
options: 500 cubits on each side (east, north, south, west)
1000 cubits long and 500 cubits wide
A circle with a diameter of 500 cubits
300 cubits square
questions.correctAnswer: 500 cubits on each side (east, north, south, west)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:16-19 details measuring the east, north, south, and west sides, each being 500 cubits (or reeds, depending on translation texts, but 500 is specified repeatedly).

questions.question: Why was the wall built all around the outside of the temple area?
options: To make a separation between the holy and the common
To defend the city against Babylon
To keep the wild beasts out
To serve as a market for the merchants
questions.correctAnswer: To make a separation between the holy and the common
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:20 (ESV): "He measured it on the four sides. It had a wall around it, 500 cubits long and 500 cubits broad, to make a separation between the holy and the common."

questions.question: What was NOT permitted to touch the people in the outer court directly from the sanctuary priests?
options: The holiness of their priestly garments
The blood of the sacrifices
The water from the basin
The showbread
questions.correctAnswer: The holiness of their priestly garments
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:14 (ESV): "They shall put on other garments before they go near to that which is for the people." (Lest they "transmit holiness" inappropriately, a concept seen elsewhere in Levitical law).

questions.question: The measuring of the exterior temple wall signifies completion of what?
options: The complete, perfectly proportioned, and divinely mandated design of the holy precinct
The end of Ezekiel's entire vision
The end of the Babylonian exile
The destruction of the earthly temple
questions.correctAnswer: The complete, perfectly proportioned, and divinely mandated design of the holy precinct
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42 concludes the architectural measuring of the temple complex before the glory of the Lord returns in chapter 43.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the northern and southern chambers in relation to the sanctuary?
options: They functioned as the operational and holy dining domains for exclusively the Zadokite priests
They were waiting rooms for the congregation
They were the treasury vaults for the king of Judah
They housed the musicians and singers of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They functioned as the operational and holy dining domains for exclusively the Zadokite priests
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 42:13: "...the holy chambers, where the priests who approach the Lord shall eat..."

key_verse_text: "He measured it on the four sides. It had a wall around it, 500 cubits long and 500 cubits broad, to make a separation between the holy and the common."
